output_text:
Prioritize Workers & Pages for new apps; use official `wrangler`. Always start with `wrangler generate`.
npx wrangler generate my-worker --type=module --ts
npx create-cloudflare@latest my-fullstack-app --framework next

Monorepos: `pnpm` or `yarn workspaces`; centralize dependencies/build scripts: `"workspaces": ["apps/*", "packages/*"]`.

Secrets: `wrangler.toml` or Cloudflare dashboard; `.dev.vars` locally; integrate with CLI tools. ❌ BAD: Storing sensitive data directly in code or `.env` files that aren't `.dev.vars`.
dotenv -e .dev.vars -- npx prisma migrate dev

Design for edge: stateless Workers; Durable Objects for stateful workloads. Workers are stateless and globally distributed. Avoid in-memory state that needs to persist across requests or instances. ❌ BAD: Relying on global variables for user sessions or shared data. Use KV for simple key-value storage, D1 for relational data, or Durable Objects for strong consistency and real-time state.

Use D1 for new serverless relational databases; Hyperdrive to accelerate existing regional databases; R2 for large files (zero egress fees, global distribution).

Secure internal services without opening firewall ports; integrate SSO for private apps. Use `cloudflared` for Azure, AWS, GCP, or on-prem access; present private web apps on Cloudflare-owned domains with SSO.
cloudflared tunnel create Azure-01

Keep Worker bundles small; tree-shake aggressively. ❌ BAD: Importing large, unoptimized libraries. Use `esbuild`
